# Seal plugin catalog reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm generate:plugin-schemas` from src/shared/plugins. Do not edit. -->

The orca-catalog.json file that lists installable plugins and their releases.

Add `"$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stablyai/orca/main/docs/schemas/plugins/orca-catalog.v2.schema.json"` to `orca-catalog.json` for completion and inline errors in your editor.
`Since` is the first Seal release that reads the field. Older releases ignore fields they do not know.

## Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$schema` | string | no | 1.4.245 | JSON Schema URL for editor completion. Ignored by Seal. |
| `catalogVersion` | `2` | yes | 1.4.245 | Catalog format. Raised only for a change older Seal cannot ignore; a newer Seal reads this one. |
| `name` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | Catalog display name. Example: `"Seal Plugins"` |
| `owner` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | Account that publishes the catalog. Example: `"stablyai"` |
| `plugins` | [CatalogEntry](#catalogentry)[] | yes | 1.4.245 | Listed plugins, at most 2048. Each `id` should appear once; Seal keeps the first. An entry this Seal cannot read is skipped, never fatal. |

## CatalogEntry

One installable plugin.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | `<publisher>.<id>`: the publisher is the repository owner, lowercased (Seal installs under this key, whatever the manifest's deprecated `publisher` says), and the id is the manifest's `id`. Each half is at most 64 characters, and the reserved names `constructor` and `prototype` are refused. Example: `"acme.gleam-syntax"` |
| `source` | [CatalogGitSource](#cataloggitsource) | yes |  | Where the plugin source lives. |
| `ownerId` | integer | no | 1.4.246 | GitHub's numeric id of the repository owner, recorded the first time the plugin was listed. Names can be renamed or re-registered; this id cannot. Informational: Seal does not read it yet, and older Seal ignores it. Example: `1234567` |
| `description` | string | no | 1.4.245 | Listing text shown in the catalog. |
| `categories` | string[] | no | 1.4.245 | Lowercase slugs used to filter the catalog, each listed once. At most 16; extras are ignored. |
| `releases` | [CatalogRelease](#catalogrelease)[] | yes | 1.4.245 | Installable releases, newest first. Seal installs the first one whose `minimumOrca` it meets, so keep older releases listed when you raise `engines.orca`. At most 32. |

## CatalogGitSource

Where the plugin source lives.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"git"` | yes | 1.4.245 | Source kind. Only `git` is supported. |
| `url` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | HTTPS or SSH URL of the plugin repository. Example: `"https://github.com/acme/orca-gleam-syntax.git"` |
| `ref` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | Branch or tag the author publishes from. Each release pins an exact commit. Example: `"main"` |
| `path` | string | no | 1.4.245 | Directory inside the repository that holds `orca-plugin.json`, so one repository can publish many plugins. Use `/` separators, with no leading `/`, `.` or `..`. Omit when the plugin is the repository root. Example: `"plugins/gleam-syntax"` |

## CatalogRelease

The exact release the catalog vouches for. Seal refuses bytes that differ.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | The manifest's `version` for this release. Example: `"1.2.0"` |
| `commit` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | Full SHA-1 commit Seal checks out for this release. |
| `contentHash` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | SHA-256 of the plugin's installed files, as Seal computes it at install. |
| `execution` | `"data"` \| `"declarative"` \| `"sandboxed-ui"` \| `"trusted-worker"` | yes | 1.4.245 | The manifest's `execution` profile. Example: `"data"` |
| `minimumOrca` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | The manifest's `engines.orca` without `>=`. Older Seal lists the plugin but will not install it. Example: `"1.4.245"` |
| `types` | (`"interface-language"` \| `"app-theme"` \| `"terminal-theme"` \| `"icon-theme"` \| `"syntax"` \| `"instructions"` \| `"panel"` \| `"editor"` \| `"worker"`)[] | no | 1.4.245 | Optional; Seal derives it from `contributes` and `execution`. When present, every kind of contribution the release carries, matching its manifest exactly. `instructions` needs the `declarative` profile or higher, `panel` and `editor` need `sandboxed-ui`, and `worker` needs `trusted-worker`. Example: `["syntax"]` |
| `name` | string | no | 1.4.245 | The manifest's `name`, so Seal can suggest the plugin before downloading it. Example: `"Gleam"` |
| `license` | string | no | 1.4.245 | SPDX license expression. Example: `"MIT"` |
| `repository` | string | no | 1.4.245 | Source repository page, https only. Seal links it when it is a github.com or gitlab.com repository of the plugin's publisher. Example: `"https://github.com/acme/orca-gleam-syntax"` |
| `sourceUnavailable` | `true` | no | 1.4.246 | Set when the release's `repository` is gone and `source` serves an archived copy, so Seal links `source` instead. Example: `true` |
| `homepage` | string | no | 1.4.245 | Project homepage, https only. Example: `"https://example.com/gleam"` |
| `updatedAt` | string | no | 1.4.245 | When this release was published, as an ISO 8601 date or date-time. Example: `"2026-10-20"` |
| `changelog` | string | no | 1.4.245 | What changed in this release, as plain text. At most 2000 characters. Example: `"Adds highlighting for use expressions."` |
| `images` | [CatalogImages](#catalogimages) | no | 1.4.245 | Images extracted from the release by catalog CI, which re-encodes them and strips metadata. Same rules as the manifest: icon PNG, WEBP, static, at least 128×128, square, at most 256 KB. Cover PNG, JPEG, WEBP, static, at least 800×500, at most 1024 KB. Screenshots PNG, JPEG, WEBP, static, at least 1280×800, at most 1536 KB. Images must not imitate Seal's trust badges. |
| `themePreview` | [CatalogThemePreview](#catalogthemepreview)[] | no | 1.4.245 | Up to 4 theme palettes for listing art. Display only; the installed theme files decide the real colors. |
| `contributes` | [CatalogContribution](#catalogcontribution)[] | no | 1.4.245 | What the release adds, as the listing shows it. Generate it with the catalog tooling; Seal refuses an install whose manifest says otherwise. |
| `capabilities` | (`"workspace:read"` \| `"workspace:write"` \| `"agent:read"` \| `"agent:launch"` \| `"terminal:send"` \| `"terminal:read"` \| `"notifications:show"` \| `"storage:own"` \| `"secrets:own"` \| `"settings:own"` \| `"appearance:write"` \| `"workspace:create"` \| `"automation:read"` \| `"automation:write"` \| `"history:read"`)[] | no | 1.4.245 | Every capability the release asks for. Seal refuses an install whose manifest asks for different ones. Example: `["notifications:show"]` |
| `fileTypes` | string[] | no | 1.4.245 | Extensions, without the dot, that this release opens. Seal suggests the plugin when such a file has no viewer. |
| `editorFileTypes` | string[] | no | 1.4.245 | The `fileTypes` this release opens in a custom editor. Seal suggests the plugin for such a file even when it already opens it as text. |

## CatalogImages

Images extracted from the release by catalog CI, which re-encodes them and strips metadata. Same rules as the manifest: icon PNG, WEBP, static, at least 128×128, square, at most 256 KB. Cover PNG, JPEG, WEBP, static, at least 800×500, at most 1024 KB. Screenshots PNG, JPEG, WEBP, static, at least 1280×800, at most 1536 KB. Images must not imitate Seal's trust badges.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | [CatalogImage](#catalogimage) | no |  | An image stored in the catalog repository. |
| `cover` | [CatalogImage](#catalogimage) | no |  | An image stored in the catalog repository. |
| `screenshots` | [CatalogImage](#catalogimage)[] | no | 1.4.245 | Screenshots, at most 6. |

## Versions and compatibility

- **What only lists is tolerant.** A catalog never decides what runs (installing re-checks the exact bytes), so Seal keeps whatever it can read: unknown keys are ignored at every level, an entry it cannot read is skipped, an invalid display-only field is dropped, a list over its limit is trimmed, and a repeated `id` keeps the first entry. Validation in CI is where these become errors.
- **The file name never changes.** `catalogVersion` (now 2) rises only for a change older clients cannot ignore; a Seal that sees a higher number refuses the catalog with "update Seal to browse this catalog" rather than misreading it.
- **Releases are a list, newest first.** Seal offers the first release whose `minimumOrca` it meets, so keep the previous release listed when a new one raises `engines.orca`; Seal shows "Needs Seal X" only when none fits.

## Publisher names and trust

- **Publisher is the repository owner.** Like a Go module path, a plugin's publisher is where it lives, never what its manifest says: the official and community catalogs set each entry's `id` to `<owner>.<manifest id>` from the GitHub user or organization that owns the repository (`acme` for `github.com/acme/gleam-syntax`), and Seal installs under that `id`. A Git URL install uses the URL's owner and a folder uses `local`. The manifest's `publisher` is deprecated and ignored. Seal does not check the owner for catalogs you add yourself; their `id` is what they say.
- **Listed names are pinned to GitHub ids.** The community catalog records the numeric owner and repository ids when a plugin is first listed, pauses new versions after a rename or transfer until Stably confirms it, and refuses a repository that was deleted and recreated under the same name. Each listed version is permanent: a moved tag never replaces it.
- **Reserved names install only from Seal's official catalog.** The publishers `stablyai`, `official`, `anthropic`, `openai`, `github` and any starting `seal` (any case), and ids starting `orca-`, are refused from any other catalog, a Git URL or a local folder. A catalog that lists one is refused whole. `pnpm validate:plugin` rejects these publishers except `stablyai`.
- **Trust comes from the catalog's address.** Seal labels a plugin with where it came from: the Official mark for Seal's catalog, otherwise the catalog's name and the owner in its Git URL (`github.com/acme`, `gitlab.com/acme/tools`), never the manifest's text. Development folders show `Dev · unverified`, Git URL installs `Unverified`.
- **An install stays with its catalog.** Seal records the catalog each plugin was installed from and updates it only from there. When another catalog lists the same id, the plugin page says so, and switching means removing the plugin and installing it again.

## One repository can hold many plugins

Give each plugin its own directory and set `source.path` to it. Seal downloads the pinned commit but installs only that directory, and `contentHash` covers only its files, so a commit that changes a sibling plugin leaves this plugin's hash, and its users, untouched. Moving a plugin to another directory counts as moving repositories: users review the update before it installs.

```json
{ "id": "acme.gleam-syntax", "source": { "kind": "git", "url": "https://github.com/acme/orca-plugins.git", "ref": "main", "path": "plugins/gleam-syntax" } }
```

Run `pnpm validate:plugin plugins/gleam-syntax` in that repository to print the directory's `path` and its release entry. Listing images stay relative to the catalog repository.

## Install links

An install link opens Seal at a plugin's page in Settings → Plugins. It never installs: the user reads the page and presses Install, and the usual review applies. If plugins are off, the page waits behind **Turn on plugins**.

```text
orca://plugins/<publisher>.<id>?catalog=<official | community | catalog Git URL>
```

- `catalog` defaults to `official`. `community` is Seal's community catalog. Any other value must be an HTTPS or SSH Git URL of at most 512 characters, read at its `main` branch, without a password or token. Seal asks **Add catalog …?** before fetching a catalog the user hasn't added, and that includes `community`.
- Reserved publishers (above) are accepted only with the official catalog. A link longer than 2048 characters, with another query parameter, or with an id that isn't `<publisher>.<id>` shows a short error and does nothing else. Repeats of the same link within a few seconds are ignored.

## Clients before format 2

Seal reads `orca-catalog.json` first and falls back to `orca-marketplace.json`. That older file is frozen: shipped clients reject any key they do not know, so it carries only `name`, `owner` and each plugin's `id`, `source`, `description` and `categories`, and leaves out plugins with a `source.path`, which those clients would install from the repository root. Generate it from `orca-catalog.json` rather than editing two files:

```sh
node config/scripts/export-legacy-plugin-catalog.mjs orca-catalog.json orca-marketplace.json
```
